title: 1% does not cost 1%
hook: One percent sounds like nothing. That is the whole trick.
description: A pure arithmetic demonstration: what a 1% annual fee does to 7% a year over 30 years. 1.06^30 / 1.07^30 = 0.7545. Not financial advice.
sources: no external claim is made in this video; figures are computed, not cited

shots.vo: One percent sounds like nothing. That is the whole trick.
shots.headline: 1% is not 1%
shots.sub: thirty years. same market. two fees.

shots.vo: Take seven percent a year. Now take one point off, every year, forever.
shots.headline: now subtract one point, every year, forever

shots.vo: After thirty years the gap is not one percent. It compounds against you.
shots.headline: Same market. Two endings.

shots.vo: At year five it is four percent. At thirty it is twenty four.
shots.headline: the gap is quiet for years
shots.sub: share of final balance lost to the one-point fee

shots.vo: You are not buying returns with that point. You are renting the wrapper.
shots.headline: the fee is not a product

left.label: The fee
left.body: charged every year, win or lose

shots.vo: Compounding does not care whose side it is on.
shots.headline: COMPOUNDING WORKS BOTH WAYS
shots.sub: in your favour, or against you

shots.vo: The fee is small. The horizon is not.
shots.quote: The fee is small. The horizon is not.

shots.vo: The question was never the fee. It is the thirty years you leave it alone.
shots.headline: Time is the multiplier
shots.sub: the fee just takes a slice of every one of them
